rejected.title: Staff and business objectives
card: A business objective is a goal the business wants to reach, such as higher sales, better customer service or lower costs.
Staff do the work that moves a business towards its objectives. A cook, a sales assistant or a driver each carries out tasks that the objectives depend on.
When staff perform well, they can lift sales, keep customers happy and use time and materials with less waste. This helps the business meet its objectives.
Staff who are poorly matched to a job may make more errors or work more slowly. This can make objectives harder to reach, so hiring the right people matters.
rejected.remember: Good staff help a business reach its goals, so choosing the right people matters.

a.q: Why does hiring the right people matter to a business?
opts: Staff who perform well help it meet its objectives
Staff who perform well remove the need for objectives
Staff are only needed once objectives have been met
Staff choose the objectives the business will set
a.why: Staff do the work that moves the business towards its goals, so good performers help it meet its objectives. Objectives are still needed to give that work direction, so staff do not replace them.
a.clue: Think about who does the work that reaches the goals.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Geelong. Her objective is to keep customers coming back. Which new hire would most help her reach it?
opts: A sales assistant who serves customers warmly and well
A sales assistant who is cheap but often rude to customers
A baker who works fast but ignores customer requests
A driver who often delivers customer orders late
b.why: A sales assistant who serves customers well keeps them happy, which supports the objective of repeat visits. The cheap but rude assistant may save on wages, but poor service can drive customers away, which works against the objective.
b.clue: Ask how each person's work would make customers feel.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Geelong. Her objective is to cut wasted ingredients this year. Which new hire would most help her reach it?
opts: A baker who measures carefully and bakes to the daily orders
A baker who bakes fast and makes extra loaves to be safe
A sales assistant who is friendly and chats with customers
A driver who is always on time and delivers to plan
b.why: Wasted ingredients come mostly from the baking, so a baker who measures and bakes to orders links most directly to the objective. The fast baker may be productive, but extra loaves go unsold and add waste. Friendly service and on-time driving are good, but they do not target this objective.
b.clue: Match the objective to the job where the waste happens.

a.best: Staff who perform well help it meet its objectives

b.best: A baker who measures carefully and bakes to the daily orders
